name: LValueData.harmonicPoly_eq_schurCoeffPoly
summary: Evaluate both polynomials at every point z: the Schur coefficient polynomial is evaluated by `eval_schurCoeffPoly`, the harmonic one by the renaming of `LValueData.toPoly_eq_rename_harmonicPoly` and `eval_toPoly`.

steps.claim: Compare the values at every point z: by `eval_schurCoeffPoly`, renaming (`eval_rename`), the Weyl evaluation of the Schur action (`schur_mulVec_weylEval`) and `LValueData.toPoly_eq_rename_harmonicPoly` with `eval_toPoly`, the two values are the same dot product.
steps.lean:
schurCoeffPoly (η ᵥ* weylGramOver) 1 := funext fun z ↦ by
  simpa +contextual [eval_schurCoeffPoly X.isLiftWeight, eval_rename, show minor (h := 1) ℂ _ =
    _ from det_unique _, weylEval, entrywise, nablaBasis_eq_one, weylGram_isSymm.apply,
    ← mulVec_transpose] using! (schur_mulVec_weylEval X.isLiftWeight.1 (z ⟨·, ·, ·⟩) 1 ▸
    X.toPoly_eq_rename_harmonicPoly η ▸ eval_toPoly .. :).trans (dotProduct_comm ..)

steps.claim: The minor of size one is the single entry (`det_unique`), and the Weyl Gram matrix is symmetric (`weylGram_isSymm`); the dot products agree after commuting.
steps.lean:
show minor (h := 1) ℂ _ =
    _ from det_unique _, weylEval, entrywise, nablaBasis_eq_one, weylGram_isSymm.apply,
    ← mulVec_transpose] using! (schur_mulVec_weylEval X.isLiftWeight.1 (z ⟨·, ·, ·⟩) 1 ▸
    X.toPoly_eq_rename_harmonicPoly η ▸ eval_toPoly .. :).trans (dotProduct_comm ..)
